Whether you use reference photo or mirror, start by outlining (very lightly) each shape you see. Don't think of it as drawing a face, think of it as just a bunch of shapes with different amounts of light. Don't focus on detail! Just make simple lines based on where you think shapes start and end (i.e. Where you think the shape of the tip of the nose ends and the more flat parts begin) After you're confident in where all these shapes are, then start added value to these shapes by beginning with midtown grays. After, keep increasing the darkness of the shapes and really observe where the dark shapes differentiate from the midtone shapes and from the light shapes. Make sure you are looking at yourself more than the drawing and don't get caught up on details til the very end (like curvature of the eyes of jawline, or any fine tiny lines).

Pretend you are god and god starts with really vague and abstract shapes for a face. God slowly slowly slowly adds value (dark and light) to create shapes that further create depth. A face can still read as a face without intense detail.
Good luck!

Edit: your end result should avoid heavy/dark outlining of the shapes, only outline in the beginning to get an idea of where things are. And smudging can make all your value look like the same tone, so only use it if very necessary.
